findings.title: Missing `key` prop for Grafana rule items rendered in a list
findings.body: In the `.map()` callback that renders `rules` (line 151), the `'datasource'` and `default` cases pass `key={key}` to the returned element, but the `'grafana'` case (lines 155-163) returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` without any `key` prop. This was present before this PR (the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` had `key={key}`) and was dropped when switching to `GrafanaRuleListItem`. Since this list grows via infinite scroll/filtering (`setRules((rules) => rules.concat(...))`), missing keys cause React warnings and make React fall back to index-based reconciliation, which can cause incorrect component reuse/state bleed between rows (e.g. open menus, pause state) when the list changes. Add `key={key}` back to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items never render when only `promRule` is supplied (new ruler-less list view)
findings.body: The Pause item (line 123-125) is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the Delete item (lines 165-175) is gated on `rulerRule` being truthy. Both `canPause` and `canDelete` are now computed as an OR between the ruler-based ability and the new Grafana-prom-rule-based ability (lines 81-87), so these booleans can be `true` purely from the `promRule` permission check. However, in the new list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` -> `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) only `promRule` is ever passed to this component; `rulerRule` is always `undefined`. As a result, Pause and Delete are computed as allowed but the menu items are unconditionally suppressed because they still require a `rulerRule` reference (`MenuItemPauseRule` needs the full rule body, and `handleDelete` is typed to take a `RulerRuleDTO`). Users browsing the new Grafana-managed alert list therefore lose the ability to pause or delete rules from the row menu, with no indication why, even though the ability checks say it should be allowed. This is also implicitly confirmed by the new test in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx which asserts exactly 4 menu items (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) with no delete/pause.

findings.title: `returnTo` query param dropped from the rule view link
findings.body: The previous `GrafanaRuleListItem` (in the now-deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the view href with `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`, so that navigating to the rule detail page preserved a way back to the originating (possibly filtered) list. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds `href: createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` with no `returnTo` parameter at all. This removes the 'back to list' behavior for every rule reached via the new list components (`GrafanaGroupLoader` and `FilterView`), which is a UX regression for users navigating from a filtered/sorted list into a rule's detail page.

findings.title: Loss of eventual-consistency handling between Ruler and Prometheus endpoints
findings.body: The previous implementation fetched both the Ruler group and the Prometheus group and used `matchRules` to render 'Creating' items (rule exists only in Ruler, not yet in Prometheus) and 'Deleting' items (rule still returned by Prometheus but already removed from Ruler), plus a warning log on persistent mismatches. This PR removes the Ruler fetch entirely and only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (line 68). Two consequences: (1) a newly created rule that hasn't yet propagated to the Prometheus rules endpoint will simply not appear in the list at all (no skeleton, no indicator, not even caught by the `!promResponse` check since the overall response is still present, just missing this specific rule/group), and (2) a rule just deleted via the Ruler API may continue to render as a fully interactive item (with Edit/View links) until the Prometheus endpoint catches up, so users can click into a rule that no longer exists. Neither scenario is handled or surfaced to the user anymore.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name referencing removed ruler-preload logic
findings.body: The comment above `if (hookOptions.populateCache)` still reads "This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX... doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded", and the local variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, even though the actual `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call was removed in this PR. The remaining code only populates the Prometheus RTK Query cache, so the comment and variable name are now inaccurate and misleading for future maintainers.

findings.title: No replacement coverage for removed eventual-consistency scenarios
findings.body: This PR deletes the previous tests that verified 'Creating' state (ruler-only rule) and 'Deleting' state (prom-only rule) behavior, as well as the `matchRules` unit tests, without adding any new tests that cover the corresponding edge cases for the new ruler-less implementation (e.g. what happens when the requested group is not yet present/returned in the Prometheus response, or when a rule was recently deleted from Ruler but is still present in the cached Prometheus response). Given `GrafanaGroupLoader` now relies solely on the Prometheus endpoint, these consistency edge cases are exactly the ones that need new coverage, but none was added.
